Lake Errock is an unincorporated lakeside community in Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) Electoral Area C, east of Deroche near Harrison Mills — not inside the City of Mission and not inside the District of Kent. The FVRD states its Area C plan area spans from the Harrison River to east of Deroche and includes Morris Valley, Harrison Mills, Lake Errock and the eastern Deroche Bench
Lake Errock has its own named district identity: the FVRD lists Electoral Area C as Sasquatch Country, covering Harrison Mills, Hemlock Valley and Lake Errock

Servicing is lot-by-lot rather than municipal: the FVRD ran a Lake Errock Neighbourhood Plan servicing feasibility study and a local sanitary servicing plan process as part of the Area C plan work, because new Lake Errock services had to be studied before growth

blocks.text: Lake Errock: rules that affect buyers

items.t: A new community plan now governs Lake Errock: the FVRD Electoral Area C Official Community Plan, Bylaw 1747, 2024, adopted September 18, 2025, includes a dedicated Lake Errock Neighbourhood Plan and replaced the former plan, Bylaw No. 0020, 1998
FVRD Zoning Bylaw No. 1638, 2021 permits one secondary suite or one accessory dwelling unit per lot, not both, in almost all electoral areas, subject to lot size and servicing

blocks.text: Lake Errock: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The community's growth debate was driven by a former gravel pit: the FVRD's project page is titled Lake Errock Gravel Pit Redevelopment, and the Harrison Rise proposal for that site included 11 three-unit multiplexes (33 dwelling units) in the material summarized by the FVRD

Fire protection here has a named local investment: the FVRD's Canada Community-Building Fund report lists a North Fraser Fire Lake Errock gear storage renovation and Lake Errock Community Park upgrades as funded projects ( Annual Expenditure Report for Reporting Year 2025.pdf).

A Morris Valley Roadside Trail Extension and Shelter is listed in the same FVRD fund report for Electoral Area C, on the road serving Lake Errock's east side ( Annual Expenditure Report for Reporting Year 2025.pdf).
School District No. 75 assigns Deroche and Dewdney elementary catchments to Hatzic Middle School, which is the middle-school path Lake Errock families check first for a specific address

The nearest hospital named on an official health page is Mission Memorial Hospital, 7324 Hurd Street, Mission, with a 25-bed medical inpatient unit, a 20-bed Patient Assessment and Transition Home unit and a 10-bed hospice

blocks.text: Lake Errock: development and new projects

items.t: Harrison Rise, 43837 and 43873 Lougheed Highway, GWEB Holdings Ltd.: rezoning application withdrawn March 7, 2025, no active rezoning at the FVRD; the proposal was folded into the Lake Errock Neighbourhood Plan process instead, status read on the FVRD page on 2026-11-03
Area C Official Community Plan, Bylaw 1747, 2024, including the Lake Errock Neighbourhood Plan: adopted by the FVRD Board on September 18, 2025, status read on 2026-11-03

Lake Errock owners pay property tax to the Province, not to a municipality, because Lake Errock is a rural area; the Province states rural owners receive their notice from the Surveyor of Taxes Office

Electoral Area C has its own FVRD sewer service area for Morris Valley (service 444 in the FVRD financial plan), which is an Area C cost structure that does not exist in Areas F or G; whether a Lake Errock lot pays it is a parcel check

Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) is the through route, west to Deroche and Mission and east across the Harrison River toward Agassiz; BC Transit and the FVRD consulted in spring 2025 on a proposed Highway 7 bus between downtown Mission and downtown Agassiz that would serve this corridor if funded
No TransLink service reaches Lake Errock; the West Coast Express commuter trains run from Mission City Station in the City of Mission, west of Deroche

blocks.text: Lake Errock: risks and due diligence

items.t: Read the lot's designation and any development permit areas in the new Bylaw 1747, 2024 Lake Errock Neighbourhood Plan schedules, because the 1998 plan's hazard and environmentally sensitive permit areas no longer govern

Confirm water source, septic or sewer connection and perc results lot by lot on Bayview Road and Malcolm Road; the FVRD's own servicing feasibility work for the neighbourhood plan is the starting document, not listing text
Check ALR status by parcel identifier number (PID) on the Agricultural Land Commission maps before assuming a second home or subdivision is possible
